thread:
Ajay Rao: thinking out loud — should we split the credential plane from the authz plane for service keys? i.e., keep a thin, fast token for runtime routing and push policies/roles to a slightly slower policy service. tradeoffs: latency vs. clarity of claims.
Taylor Kim: like a dual-token model? short-lived runtime token + policy lookup token?
Maria Chen: +1 on separation but worried about migration. customers with long-lived API keys (hosted) will need a graceful path. also KMS rotation implications.
Liam O'Connor: short-lived tokens + a broker exchange feels right for inter-service calls. avoids exploding permission graph in every request.
Priya Patel: note: Dedicated/Private customers may insist on agent-side enforcement (no external policy calls). we need an offline-mode plan.
Ajay Rao: good point. maybe default: runtime token contains minimal claims (actor, id, scope-id) and runtime side does cache lookups. fallback to policy service when cache miss.
Taylor Kim: cache-first sounds good to keep p99 down. we should define canonical minimal claims to keep token size small.
Maria Chen: proposal for minimal JWT payload (example):
```
{
  "iss": "redwood",
  "sub": "svc:payments:1234",
  "scp": "pj:9876",
  "exp": 1712345678,
  "k":"v1"
}
```
Use a compact `scp` encoding like `org:123|pj:9876` or numeric mappings to keep tokens small.
Liam O'Connor: numeric mapping + dictionary in the gateway is best for bandwidth. also helps in TLS client-cert mode for private installs.
Priya Patel: migration ops question: how do we map existing API keys to new claims? we can't force rotation for all customers.
Ajay Rao: plan: compatibility shim in auth service that issues ephemeral runtime tokens when presented with legacy API key. TTL short, audit logged. deprecate long-lived access in 6-12 months.
Maria Chen: I'll prototype a token-adapter service that: accepts legacy key, validates, emits ephemeral jwt, logs audit event, supports HSM signing.
Taylor Kim: we should keep runtime verification to a single header check + local cache hit. if cache miss, gate calls to policy service with batch fetch. avoid per-request remote RBAC eval.
Priya Patel: RBAC nuance — do we encode role graph in the claims or reference a role-id? encoding graph duplicates source of truth. reference id + gateway cache seems safer.
Liam O'Connor: agree. reference ids + short-lived membership stamps. also consider a delta feed for gateways so they can pre-populate caches.
sec-bot: runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/authn-plane-separation (added checklist entry: "token-adapter smoke tests") :white_check_mark:
Ajay Rao: next steps: 1) Maria prototype token-adapter, 2) Taylor run perf sims for cache hit/miss, 3) Priya draft customer migration playbook, 4) Liam design delta feed API. meet to review RFC follow-up wednesday 10am?
Taylor Kim: Wednesday 10 works for me. I'll add perf goals (p99 <= 30ms on gateway path). :thumbsup:
Maria Chen: ok i'll start proto and share a minimal swagger for the adapter by EOW.
Priya Patel: I'll draft migration stages and risk matrix.
Liam O'Connor: will sketch delta feed and numeric-id registry this week.
Ajay Rao: thanks team — want to avoid overloading inference gateway. keeping the runtime token minimal + cache-first policy checks seems like the right balance. we'll capture tradeoffs in the RFC follow-up.
